title: Lift regular closed-fibre kernel parameters preserving the base regular sequence
statement: Let R and S be regular local rings, E a regular local ring, u:R→S and v:S→E local ring maps, and v surjective. Suppose v annihilates m_R S, the images of some regular system of parameters of R extend to a regular system of parameters of S, and S/m_R S is regular local. Then there is a proper ideal J of S with ker(v)=J+m_R S and a regular system of parameters t of R whose images form a regular sequence on S/J. No completeness or formal smoothness is assumed or concluded.

source.place: Tag 07NR, proof, first two paragraphs; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07NR

proof.text: Descend v to a surjective ring map B=S/m_R S → E using hkill. Identify E with B/ker by the first isomorphism theorem and transport its regular-local instance. Apply the regular-local quotient kernel parameter theorem to obtain an initial segment xbar of a regular parameter system of B generating that kernel.

source.place: Tag 07NR, proof, first two paragraphs; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07NR

proof.text: Lift the kernel parameters to S. Every lift is in ker v because v annihilates m_R S. The given extension of the R-parameters gives independent cotangent classes for their images in S. The quotient S→B identifies the residue fields, and m_R S is generated by the images of the base parameters. Its image in the cotangent space of S is therefore exactly their residue-field span. The cotangent space of B is m_S/(m_S²+m_R S); independence of the xbar classes in it therefore makes the lifted classes independent modulo the span of the base classes. Extend their union to a basis and lift the remaining vectors. Nakayama and the regular-local cotangent dimension equality make the resulting list a regular system of parameters in S.

source.place: Tag 07NR, proof, first two paragraphs; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07NR

proof.text: Let J be generated by the lifted xbar. Its sum with m_R S is ker v: subtract a linear combination of the lifts from any kernel element to obtain an element of m_R S, using the generator equality in B. In particular J is proper, since v maps to a nonzero ring. Permute the full parameter system to put x first, followed by the R-parameters. The regular-sequence and initial-quotient theorem makes S/J regular local and the remaining parameter images a regular sequence. Its initial segment consisting of the R-parameter images is regular, giving the assertion. Empty lists are covered by the same construction.

mathlib_searches.query: Lift the kernel parameters of a regular closed fibre of a map of regular local rings while keeping the base parameters a regular sequence on the quotient

lean.statement:
theorem exists_regular_fiber_kernel_parameter_quotient
    (R S : Type u) (E : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing E]
    [IsRegularLocalRing R] [IsRegularLocalRing S] [IsRegularLocalRing E]
    (u : R →+* S) (v : S →+* E) [IsLocalHom u] [IsLocalHom v]
    (hv : Function.Surjective v)
    (hkill : (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map u ≤ RingHom.ker v)
    (hparams : ∃ (t : List R) (z : List S),
      IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParameters t ∧
      IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParameters (t.map u ++ z))
    (hfiber : IsRegularLocalRing (S ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map u)) :
    ∃ J : Ideal S, J ≠ ⊤ ∧
      RingHom.ker v = J ⊔ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map u ∧
      ∃ t : List R, IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParameters t ∧
        RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular (S ⧸ J)
          (t.map ((Ideal.Quotient.mk J).comp u))
